record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Characterize those measure-preserving automorphisms T of ([0,1], λ) for which there exists another measure-preserving automorphism S with T = S^2 = S ∘ S. The paper also records the conjecture that the set of such T is Σ^1_1-complete.

evidence.quote: Problem 43 (Halmos, 1956). What T ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) has S ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) with T = S^2 = S ◦ S? Conjecture: {T ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) : ∃S ∈ Aut([0, 1], λ) T = S^2} is Σ1_1-complete.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $([0,1], \lambda)$ denote the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure, and let $\mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $([0,1], \lambda)$ (identifying automorphisms that agree $\lambda$-almost everywhere). 

(a) Give an intrinsic characterization of those $T \in \mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda)$ that admit a square root, i.e., those $T$ for which there exists $S \in \mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda)$ with $T = S \circ S$.

(b) Prove or disprove that the set
$$\{T \in \mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda) : \exists S \in \mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda),\ T = S^2\}$$
is a $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_1$-complete subset of the Polish space $\mathrm{Aut}([0,1], \lambda)$.
artifact.category_tag: Ergodic theory: square roots of measure-preserving transformations
artifact.status_search_result: The square-root problem originates with Halmos (1942/1956). Partial results are known: e.g., Chacon showed not every weakly mixing transformation has a square root, and many sufficient/necessary conditions exist for special classes (Bernoulli, ergodic with discrete spectrum, etc.). However, no general intrinsic characterization of automorphisms admitting a measure-preserving square root is known, and the conjectured $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_1$-completeness of the set of such $T$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Square Roots of Measure Preserving Transformations
status_evidence.snippet: Halmos's 1942 paper introducing the square-root problem for measure-preserving transformations.
status_evidence.claim: The square-root problem for measure-preserving transformations was posed by Halmos.

status_evidence.title: On the Root Problem in Ergodic Theory (Ornstein)
status_evidence.snippet: Ornstein and others gave partial results on the root problem, including counterexamples for weakly mixing transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known; no general characterization has been given.
